subject: Newton Accelerator packaging: voucher stacking and seed cohort discount exception
messages:
From: Alina Torres <alina@newtonaccelerator.org>

Cc: procurement@newtonaccelerator.org
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Newton: cohort voucher stacking + reserved discount inquiry

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by Redwood's low latency for interactive sessions. We're getting our seed cohort lined up and want to make sure the offer we present is simple for founders. Two asks from our side: 

1) Can Newton vouchers (the sandbox vouchers you offered earlier) be stacked with a short-term reserved-capacity discount if a cohort cohort of 25 founders converts within 60 days? We want to present a single package to sponsors.

2) Is there room for a one-time promotional uplift (10–20% additional free compute credit) for founders who sign up during demo week, without changing the billing cadence for the sponsor?

I've attached the term sheet draft and a rough SOW so you can see timelines. Procurement is copied for any contract-level questions.

Appreciate any guidance on packaging and whether we need a commercial carveout to make this work.

—Alina

Subject: Re: Newton: cohort voucher stacking + reserved discount inquiry

Hi Alina — thanks for the materials, I skimmed the SOW and term sheet and looped in Ben (pricing) and Marissa (program ops). Quick thoughts: 

- Voucher stacking: technically feasible if we treat the vouchers as pre-paid credits that can be applied at account level and then allow an additional short-lived promo bucket. Two operational caveats: 1) voucher redemptions that convert to reserved capacity complicate billing reconciliation; 2) sponsor-facing invoice must show clearly which line items are promotional credit vs committed spend.

- Promo uplift: we can attach a timebound promo code that converts to an account-level credit. For 10–20% we'd want clear eligibility gating (signed + onboarding completed within X days) to avoid broader misuse.

Ben — can you outline the preferred commercial path (voucher + promo + reserved commit) and what approvals we'd need to offer a 15% uplift for demo-week signups? Marissa — any ops red flags for cohort size ~25 and a 60-day conversion window?

Thanks,
Olga

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Ben — can you outline the preferred commercial path (voucher + promo + reserved commit) and what approvals we'd need to offer a 15% uplift for demo-week signups?

Summary of recommended commercial paths (pricing options, pick one):

Option A — Voucher + Promo (no reserved commit):
- Vouchers redeemable as account credits against hosted usage.
- Add a one-time promo credit equal to 15% of voucher value for founders who onboard within 14 days.
- Pros: simple, low ops friction.
- Cons: sponsor can't claim committed-discount pricing; no guaranteed revenue.

Option B — Voucher -> Reserved conversion window (preferred for sponsor):
- Founders redeem vouchers to create accounts. If 25 accounts convert to a reserved-commit within 60 days, sponsor receives retrospective reserved discount applied as a credit on the next invoice.
- We accept retrospective conversion only if sponsor signs a simple commitment addendum up-front.
- Pros: gives sponsor price predictability.
- Cons: requires accounting treatment for retrospective discounts and a brief hold on invoice finalization; ops will need to track conversions carefully.

Option C — Cohort Pledge + Upfront Sponsor Discount (enterprise path):
- Sponsor signs a short-term reserved commitment for cohort (e.g., $X/month for 3 months) at a discounted rate; vouchers applied on top.
- Pros: clean billing, minimal retrospective bookkeeping.
- Cons: sponsor needs to commit capital up-front.

Approvals: anything that modifies standard promo % above 10% needs RevOps and Finance sign-off. For a 15% uplift limited to demo-week and gated to onboarding <14 days, I can provisionally approve pending final RevOps approval and an explicit sponsor addendum.

Operational notes: we should include a clear fallback clause that if sponsor does not reach conversion thresholds within 60 days, promotional credits are non-refundable and expire after 90 days. That reduces accounting complexity.

Ben
Director, Growth | Redwood Inference
[internal note: escalate 15% uplift request to RevOps (revops@redwoodinference.com) and Finance for final approval]

Hi Olga / Ben / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the three options. Procurement looked at Option B and asked for two clarifications before they can sign the addendum: 

1) Can the retrospective reserved discount be shown as a line-item credit with a clear audit trail (HubSpot / invoice reference)? We need that for sponsor accounting.
2) If the sponsor signs the commitment addendum, are promotional uplift credits (the 15%) treated as separate from sponsor-committed spend for purposes of reporting and tax treatment?

If both answers are affirmative, they are comfortable moving forward with Option B and the 60-day window. We can sign a one-page addendum and route for e-signature.

Next steps: if you confirm the accounting display and credit separation, I'll send a signature-ready version of the addendum this week.

Best,
Alina
